a2-unit-05.05.1 Online class:
Tom: OK, let's read the email from your cousin together. Can you read the first sentence, please?
Ana: Sure. Life in Orlando is great, but the weather is very... how do you say the next word?
Tom: Humid.
Ana: Humid. What does humid mean?
Tom: It means the air is hot and wet. Like Rio de Janeiro in the summer.
Ana: Ah, OK. Can we say Orlando has a lot of humid?
Tom: Good question, but no. Humid is an adjective. The noun is humidity, so you can say Orlando has a lot of humidity.
Ana: Got it. And here. Last weekend I got a terrible sunburn at Cocoa Beach. What kind of word is sunburn?
Tom: It's a noun. It means red and painful skin after too much sun.
Ana: Ouch! How do you spell it? Is it one word or two?
Tom: One word. S-U-N-B-U-R-N.
Ana: And in the photo, what do you call this white cream on her face?
Tom: That's sunscreen. You put it on before you go to the beach.
Ana: Carol really needs more sunscreen! I have one more question. How do you pronounce this word? R-E-C-E-I-P-T.
Tom: Receipt. The P is silent.
Ana: A silent P? English spelling is crazy!
Tom: It is sometimes! Now cover the email. Can you remember how to spell humid?
Ana: H-U-M-I-D.
Tom: Perfect. Well done!
